entry.title: How I Made My First $1,300 from a SaaS While Finishing High School
entry.summary:
I'm 17. I made $1,300 from my SaaS in the first 30 days while juggling AP exams and college apps. Not life-changing money. But it's proof that you don't need: A tech accelerator Months of planning A perfect product Even to be out of high school You just need to move fast. I see this constantly: "I've been building my SaaS for 8 months" "Just need a few more features before launch" "Building in stealth mode" These people are building the wrong thing. They just don't know it yet because they haven't talked to a customer. I DMed 50+ people before writing a single line of code. The script: Hey [name], Saw you're working on [their project]. Built [tool name] - basically [one sentence value prop]. Solves [specific pain point]. Interested in trying it when ready? Takes 2 min to set up. Results: 50 DMs → 12 responses → 8 said yes → 5 became paying customers (from there rinse and repeat) The key: Personal + specific + clear value + low commitment My SaaS v1:
YES - Docs (existed) Rule: If you can fake it or do it manually for the first 10 customers, fake it. Pre-launch (3 days before): Posted tease on Twitter DMed 15 interested people Prepared Product Hunt assets Launch day: Posted on Product Hunt at 12:01am PT Shared everywhere (Twitter, IH, relevant communities) Responded to every comment in <15min Results: 120 signups in first 3 days 15 converted to paid in first week
$225 MRR by Day 7 Hit $1.3k MRR by Day 30 1. Building features users didn't ask for 2. Underpricing 3. Trying to please everyone I documented everything: the validation framework, DM scripts, MVP breakdown, pricing strategy, launch playbook, tools I use (~$100/mo total), and what to avoid. Free download: https://1kfounderplaybook.framer.website/ Currently using the same playbook to launch repo20 (dependency monitoring that catches breaking changes before they break production). Launching next week. We'll see if it works twice. Questions? Drop them below. Happy to share more about any part of this process.

entry.summary:
The Problem
Payment webhooks from Stripe, Apple, and Google are revenue-critical, but they're tricky to handle correctly. entry.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
entry.summary: Nous Research, the open-source artificial intelligence startup backed by crypto venture firm Paradigm, released a new competitive programming model on Monday that it says matches or exceeds several larger proprietary systems — trained in just four days using 48 of Nvidia's latest B200 graphics processors. The model, called NousCoder-14B, is another entry in a crowded field of AI coding assistants, but arrives at a particularly charged moment: Claude Code, the agentic programming tool from rival Anthropic, has dominated social media discussion since New Year's Day, with developers posting breathless testimonials about its capabilities. The simultaneous developments underscore how quickly AI-assisted software development is evolving — and how fiercely companies large and small are competing …

entry.title: The creator of Claude Code just revealed his workflow, and developers are losing their minds
entry.summary:
When the creator of the world's most advanced coding agent speaks, Silicon Valley doesn't just listen — it takes notes. For the past week, the engineering community has been dissecting a thread on X from Boris Cherny, the creator and head of Claude Code at Anthropic. What began as a casual sharing of his personal terminal setup has spiraled into a viral manifesto on the future of software development, with industry insiders calling it a watershed moment for the startup.
"If you're not reading the Claude Code best practices straight from its creator, you're behind as a programmer," wrote Jeff Tang, a prominent voice in the developer community.
